name: architecture-debate
description: Three engineers argue about splitting a monolith. Exercises deliberation graphs: positions, arguments, counter-arguments, a decision.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Okay so the thing on the table is whether we split the billing code out of the monolith before the Q4 launch or after.

utterances.speaker: Tom
utterances.text: Before. If we wait until after launch we are doing surgery on a system that is taking real money.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: That is the argument I keep hearing but I want to know what the actual pain is today. What breaks because billing is in the monolith?

utterances.speaker: Dana
utterances.text: Deploy coupling mostly. Every billing change waits on the full test suite, that is forty minutes, and if anyone else's change is red we are blocked.

utterances.speaker: Tom
utterances.text: And the blast radius. A bad migration in the orders table took billing down for two hours in June.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Right, but splitting it does not fix that. If billing still reads the orders table over the network it is the same coupling with more latency.

utterances.speaker: Dana
utterances.text: That is fair. The split only helps if we also own the data. Which means an events feed from orders into billing.

utterances.speaker: Tom
utterances.text: So now we are building a service and an event pipeline before launch. That is not a two week job.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: How long realistically?

utterances.speaker: Dana
utterances.text: Six weeks with two people if nothing surprises us. Which it will.

utterances.speaker: Tom
utterances.text: Then before launch is dead. We do not have six weeks.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Unless there is a cheaper version. What if we only fix the deploy coupling? Separate the test suite, separate the deploy pipeline, keep it in the same repo and the same database.

utterances.speaker: Dana
utterances.text: A modular monolith basically. That gets us the forty minute problem solved in maybe a week.

utterances.speaker: Tom
utterances.text: It does not get us blast radius.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: No. But blast radius happened once in six months and the deploy pain happens every day.

utterances.speaker: Tom
utterances.text: Once, that we noticed. I would want to actually count the incidents before I accept that framing.

utterances.speaker: Dana
utterances.text: I can pull that from the incident log this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Do that. But my instinct is we do the module boundary now, we do the events feed after launch, and the actual process split is a Q1 conversation.

utterances.speaker: Tom
utterances.text: My worry with that is the module boundary never becomes a service boundary. We have three modules in that repo that were supposed to be services.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: That is a real pattern, yes.

utterances.speaker: Dana
utterances.text: We could make it harder to backslide. If the module can only talk to the rest of the code through one interface file, and there is a lint rule enforcing it, then the split later is mechanical.

utterances.speaker: Tom
utterances.text: That I would accept. The lint rule is the thing that makes me believe it.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: So: module boundary plus an enforced interface, before launch. Events feed and process split deferred to Q1, revisited with incident data.

utterances.speaker: Dana
utterances.text: And I bring incident counts to Thursday so we know if the blast radius argument is worth more than we are giving it.

utterances.speaker: Tom
utterances.text: Works for me.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: One thing we have not talked about is who owns billing after the split. If it is a service it needs an on call rotation and we are six people.

utterances.speaker: Dana
utterances.text: That is an argument for staying in the monolith honestly. Two services and six people is already thin.

utterances.speaker: Tom
utterances.text: Then that goes in the Q1 discussion too. It is not a launch blocker.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Agreed. Let us stop there.
